text:
sanjay: Observed repeated pod churn on gpu-pool-us-west-2 this morning. Lots of pods being scheduled, then evicted within seconds. Looks like a backfill/spot spill pattern.

anya: Seen the alerts. Node autoscaler spun up spots in az-a then pods got moved to az-b and failed NVMe attach? 

leo: Can you paste the kube-scheduler logs around the eviction time?

sanjay: Pasting snippet from controller logs: 
```
I0318 07:12:02.123456 1 scheduler_predicate.go:210] Predicates passed for pod/train-job-xyz on node/gpu-az-a-12
I0318 07:12:03.987654 1 binder.go:143] Binding pod/train-job-xyz to node/gpu-az-a-12
I0318 07:12:04.001213 1 eviction_manager.go:102] Evicting pod/train-job-xyz: node.kubernetes.io/insufficient_ephemeral_storage
I0318 07:12:04.001345 1 scheduler_binder.go:198] Pod train-job-xyz evicted due to resource pressure
```

maria: Eviction reason shows ephemeral_storage pressure, but our monitoring shows disk usage at ~60%. Could be transient when NVMe device attach happens and kubelet reports pressure.

anya: Also saw network attach errors in cloud-provider logs: `AttachVolume failed: device not ready` for the EBS-like volume we use for TMP. Timing aligns with AZ failover from spot termination.

leo: So flow is: cluster-autoscaler scales up spots, scheduler backfills pods onto new nodes, then AWS moves/terminates spot nodes or cross-az scheduling causes volume attach failures -> kubelet reports pressure/breaks -> eviction -> reschedule -> thrash.

sanjay: Exactly. The churn amplifies fragmentation since free GPUs get transiently locked by pending pods, then freed, leaving small leftovers. Binpacking scoring is too eager to backfill.

anya: Quick mitigation we tried: set `topologySpreadConstraints` to prefer same-az for heavy IO jobs and increase `podDisruptionBudget` minAvailable to 1 for long-running training jobs. Helps a bit but doesn't stop new spots from being used.

leo: Longer-term: adjust scheduler scoring plugin parameters to penalize cross-az binding when volumes are used, or use `nodeSelector` + `zone` topology for these stateful pods. Also consider delaying hard binding until volumes attach confirmed.

maria: Could we change the binpacking scoring to prefer consolidating onto existing on-demand nodes and only use spots for opportunistic jobs? Right now CA uses mixed-instances but scheduler chooses any node that fits.

sanjay: I propose three steps: 1) Quick: introduce a soft taint `prefer-no-spots=true:NoSchedule` with a toleration TTL for critical jobs so they avoid newly created spot nodes by default. 2) Medium: tweak scheduler scoring to include a volume-attach-success metric (or prefer nodes with attached TMP volumes). 3) Long: implement a tiny controller that marks a node ReadyOnlyUntilVolumesAttached and blocks binding until cloudprovider signals attachments.

anya: For (1) we can push a mutating hook that adds tolerations to job templates where label `workload=training` is present. Low risk.

leo: For (2) we could add a custom scheduler extender or change `NodePreferAvoidPods` behavior. But that's heavier. Also consider adding a small cooldown window after node creation where it's marked `preferavoid: true` so backfill is suppressed for X seconds.

maria: Can we also lower kubelet eviction threshold for ephemeral storage? That seems risky. Maybe instead make the eviction condition check a rolling average so short spikes don't evict immediately.

ops-bot: Autogenerated note: cluster-autoscaler terminated instance i-0a1b2c3d in us-west-2a at 07:10 UTC (spot interruption signal).

sanjay: Action items: 
- anya: deploy mutating webhook to add tolerations for training jobs (quick).
- leo: prototype scheduler scoring tweak / cooldown (medium).
- maria: audit storage attach timing and see if we can make kubelet attach confirmation explicit (long).

anya: I'll get the webhook PR up by EOD and add a feature flag so we can rollback.

leo: I'll run a sim with the scoring tweak on a staging cluster and measure eviction rate vs packing efficiency.

maria: I'll correlate cloud attach failures with eviction timestamps and file an infra bug if attach latency > 10s.

sanjay: Also let's add a descheduler job that consolidates tiny leftover GPU allocations every 6 hours to reduce fragmentation. We can keep low-frequency to avoid extra churn.

anya: agree. For the descheduler config I recommend `RemoveDuplicates` + `LowNodeUtilization` tuned for GPUs. Example job snippet: 
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: gpu-descheduler
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: descheduler
        image: k8s.gcr.io/descheduler:latest
        args: ["--policy-config-file=/policy.yaml"]
```

leo: Nice. One more thought: add a metric `scheduler.backfill_score` so we can A/B test scoring changes without full rollout.

sanjay: Good call. Let's reconvene tomorrow after PRs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

anya: cc @platform-oncall FYI
